title: Rockenfeller inherits Zandvoort Race 2 after Wittmann is disqualified
dek: Mike Rockenfeller, who started seventh, was declared winner of DTM Race 2 at Zandvoort for Audi after Marco Wittmann, first across the line, was disqualified when no fuel sample could be taken.

chapters.title: BMW arrive for Sunday with a weight advantage
text: Saturday had belonged to BMW. Timo Glock won Race 1 from pole by 0.178s from his team-mate Marco Wittmann, with Maxime Martin third, and René Rast took the championship lead from Mattias Ekström by one point, 114 to 113, with ninth place after Ekström's trip through the gravel.

The BMWs went into Sunday 15kg lighter than the Audis and Mercedes under the series' performance weights, a system that had long been a source of controversy. Mercedes, at its first race weekend since announcing its exit from the DTM at the end of 2018, had left Saturday without a podium.

chapters.title: Farfus on pole, and two drivers thrown out
text: BMW dominated the second qualifying session as well. Augusto Farfus set 1m27.475s for pole, worth three bonus points, with Wittmann 0.141s slower and Martin 0.167s behind, putting three BMWs on the front two rows. Jamie Green was fourth on 1m27.673s, the best of the Audis, followed by Rast on 1m27.832s in sixth and Mike Rockenfeller seventh on 1m27.892s. Gary Paffett's 1m27.926s was the best Mercedes time. Ekström could manage only 12th on 1m28.089s, and Lucas Auer 13th.

The session was overshadowed by penalties. Edoardo Mortara got in the way of Glock on a quick lap, and Glock responded by deliberately blocking the Mercedes in return. The stewards disqualified Glock from qualifying for the incident and fined him €3,000 for unsporting behaviour, while Mortara was penalised for blocking as well. Glock's 1m27.690s would have been fifth-quickest, and Paffett's time was struck out too, because a tyre from outside his allocation had been fitted to his car. Paul di Resta took no part in the session.

chapters.title: Wittmann takes the lead before the first corner
text: Farfus made a poor start and Wittmann went round him before the first corner to lead. Martin, third on the grid, barely moved off the line and dropped far down the order, and Rast also got away slowly, which opened a chance for Ekström. Rockenfeller moved up behind the leading BMW, and with some cars, Farfus among them, making their mandatory stop in the first laps, Wittmann led Rockenfeller after the first lap.
Bruno Spengler had a five-second penalty for a jump start to serve at his stop. Rast's afternoon ended early with damage to his Audi. Di Resta was also among the drivers who did not finish.

chapters.title: Duval stays out while the leaders stop
text: BMW waited until Wittmann's lap times fell away before calling him in, and Audi reacted in the same way with its front-runners. Only Loïc Duval, who had started 15th, was left out for far longer than anyone else, a gamble that would pay off at the end of the race.

Wittmann kept the lead after his stop and Rockenfeller, who had taken second, followed him back out onto the track. With Duval still to stop, he led the race on the road while everyone else had already changed tyres.

chapters.title: Ekström's slow puncture and a train behind him
text: Ekström had worked his way up to third on the road behind Wittmann and Rockenfeller, but his pace fell away. He later reported falling pressure in his left-front tyre and said that he had been driving almost on the rim at the end. Müller, just behind him, defended Ekström's position while Paffett tried to get through.

Duval finally made his stop late in the race and rejoined third, while Wittmann, whose tyres were wearing, saw Rockenfeller close up but could not find a way past. The fight for the minor places was tight: on the last lap Paffett and Martin both tried to get past Müller, who held them off even when the Mercedes and the BMW attacked on different lines.

chapters.title: Rockenfeller is winner after a two-hour wait
text: Wittmann crossed the line first after 37 laps, with Rockenfeller close behind and Duval third on the road. About two hours later the BMW was disqualified from the result: after the race it was held in parc fermé, and the 1kg sample of residual fuel required by the regulations could not be taken. Rockenfeller, who had started seventh, was promoted to the win in 56m33.404s, with Duval second, 16.581s back after starting 15th. Duval also set the fastest lap, a 1m29.168s on lap 28.

Ekström was third, 58.073s behind the winner, followed by Müller, who had started 16th, and Paffett in fifth. Ekström, Müller, Paffett, Martin, Glock and Farfus crossed the line within two seconds of one another. Martin was sixth after his poor start, Glock seventh and Farfus eighth from pole, with Green ninth and Spengler tenth. Auer finished a lap down in 14th, and Wickens completed 33 laps.

chapters.title: Ekström extends his lead as Wittmann loses the win
text: Wittmann had celebrated what he thought was his first win of the season for roughly two hours before the news came. He said afterwards that he was speechless and very disappointed, but accepted the decision and said BMW would attack again at the Nürburgring. BMW's sporting director Jens Marquardt promised a full analysis. Wittmann dropped to eighth in the standings on 93 points.

Audi inherited the top four places: Rockenfeller and Duval gave Audi Sport Team Phoenix a one-two, with Ekström and Müller of Abt Sportsline third and fourth. For Duval, who had had no points before the weekend, second place meant 18 in a single afternoon. Rockenfeller moved up to 110 points, third in the standings.

In the championship Ekström regained the lead on 128 points, 14 clear of Rast on 114, who scored nothing on Sunday. Rockenfeller was third, ahead of Glock on 104, Martin on 102 and Auer and Green on 99 each. Ekström said he had noticed early that air was missing from his left-front tyre. Paffett complained about Audi's team tactics in the closing laps, while Müller said the last-lap fight was fair, with no contact.

Mercedes left Zandvoort without a point from Auer in either race and with di Resta and Wickens among the retirements, the best Mercedes result being Paffett's fifth. Glock, who recovered to seventh despite the qualifying penalty, moved to 104 points. The next round is the Nürburgring on 9–10 September, three weeks away, with six races left in the season.

facts.v: Rockenfeller started seventh and was promoted to winner in 56m33.404s after Wittmann was disqualified.

one.label: BMW's Marco Wittmann disqualified from Zandvoort DTM win

facts.v: Wittmann's BMW was disqualified because the required 1kg sample of residual fuel could not be taken.

one.label: DTM: BMW mit zu wenig Benzin - Marco Wittmann disqualifiziert!

facts.v: Ekström went to 128 points, 14 ahead of Rast, with Rockenfeller third on 110.
Glock was disqualified from qualifying for blocking Mortara, and Paffett for fitting a tyre outside his allocation.
RMG team principal Stefan Reinhold said the team had made a mistake in handling the refuelling equipment.
